pr_title: Fix missing case for function pointer signatures in Crossgen2
pr_body:
As Andy Ayers conjectured in the issue #72822 and I confirmed,
Crossgen2 signature emitter was missing the code path for
emitting function pointer signatures. This change fixes this
deficiency. The change also removes the issues.targets exclusion
of the affected test that Andy originally merged in to mitigate
the issue.

Thanks

Tomas

P.S. Even though MethodSignatureFlags more or less corresponds
to CoreCLR runtime calling convention, I have ignored this fact
and implemented an explicit conversion as I find it cleaner, please
let me know if you think otherwise. I would also appreciate
double-checking of the logic around Static vs. HASTHIS as I'm not
completely sure about the exact interpretation of this runtime flag.

/cc @dotnet/crossgen-contrib 

Fixes: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/72822
pr_comments:

and implemented an explicit conversion as I find it cleaner,

review_comments: Does this need to emit modops / modreqs, or are those intentionally skipped here?

Well, we probably do, I'll try to fix this but the problem is that apparently there's no pre-existing coverage for function pointer signatures in CoreCLR testing so I guess I'll need to create some dedicated tests to verify this works as expected especially as this is the first place in Crossgen2 where we'll be emitting these signature modifiers.
Actually - if we are ever only going to use signature to create type handle at runtime, we should not need to emit the modopts/modreqs. They are not part of the type handle at runtime.
Also, the function pointer support in reflection is broken and inconsistent in various ways today. We hope to fix that as part of https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/69273 in .NET 8.
That's exactly why I asked for a broad review, this is obviously new functionality with very limited test coverage (amounting to the one JIT test I'm re-enabling in this PR).

We have logic to handle emission of modopts/modreqs, but that should only be needed for function signatures, and those are already handled correctly so far as I'm aware. For this support I do not believe we need to handle modreqs/modopts at all, ever.
